media_work.title: Witch Hunt
media_work.focus_or_theme: Examines the Bakersfield/Kern County child abuse cases of the 1980s, where dozens of people (mostly parents and daycare workers) were accused and convicted of bizarre ritualistic abuse amid the "Satanic Panic." Narrated by Sean Penn, it highlights the mass hysteria and resulting wrongful convictions.
media_work.summaryNotes: At least 36 people were convicted in Kern County based on these allegations; 34 convictions were later overturned. Sentences totaled over 1000 years in some initial cases (e.g., McCuans/Kniffens).

media_item.focus_or_theme: Examines the Bakersfield/Kern County child abuse cases of the 1980s, where dozens of people (mostly parents and daycare workers) were accused and convicted of bizarre ritualistic abuse amid the "Satanic Panic."
media_item.summary_notes: The documentary features interviews with wrongfully convicted individuals and their families, archival footage from the era, analysis of flawed investigative techniques, and commentary on the "Satanic Panic" phenomenon. It explores the mass hysteria and resulting wrongful convictions in Bakersfield/Kern County.
key_quotes_raw: Likely features interviews with the wrongfully convicted individuals and their families, archival footage from the era, analysis of the flawed investigative techniques, and commentary on the "Satanic Panic" phenomenon. Sean Penn's narration provides context.
systemic_issues_raw: Dangers of moral panic and mass hysteria influencing the justice system
Unreliability of child testimony obtained through suggestive or coercive methods
Importance of scientific/evidence-based investigations vs. hysteria
Devastating long-term consequences of wrongful convictions fueled by public fear
policy_recommendations_raw: Implicitly warns against repeating history by succumbing to moral panics and highlights the need for rigorous, evidence-based standards in child abuse investigations and prosecutions.

external_links_raw.description: Resources on proper forensic interviewing techniques for children (e.g., NICHD protocol)

featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Multiple individuals were wrongfully convicted in Kern County in the mid-1980s, primarily for child sexual abuse based on flawed investigations and mass hysteria.  Many convictions were overturned in the mid-1990s after years of imprisonment. The cases highlight the dangers of moral panic and unreliable child testimony.
contributing_factors_raw: Mass hysteria ("Satanic Panic", Day Care Sex Abuse Hysteria)
Flawed and highly suggestive child interview techniques
Coaching/contamination of child testimony
Lack of physical evidence
Prosecutorial zeal
Influence of questionable "expert" theories and training materials on investigators
